rationale: The variant experiment executed in a clean copy (6e187216178a49d4ae02bd8c2afaeaf9, completed, exit 0) with all seventeen comparisons complete and evaluated: proposing a configuration change through the re-added voter was held pending exactly like an ordinary proposal and no node applied it, while the rest of the lineage's observations reproduced unchanged. This update attributes the retained interpretation to that experiment, records the configuration-proposal observation as durable knowledge with receipt indices, and removes the limitation that the administrative entry point had not been executed.

investigations.hypothesis: node.run() keeps its proposal gate armed only as a side effect of observing a leader change and disarms it when the local member is removed from the configuration; a re-admission does not re-arm it, so while no leader change is observed the member's MsgProp traffic (Node.Propose and Node.ProposeConfChange) stays pending on the non-nil n.propc channel instead of being forwarded, appended, or rejected with an error. Retained evidence (six-signal lineage): with the leader unchanged the invocation does not return inside the observed windows, payloads are not committed, an invocation with a context that never expires stays pending, the same call succeeds and commits once leadership changes, and a never-removed member's proposals commit throughout.
investigations.discriminator: Drive a real three-node Node-API cluster (config {1,2,3}, leader 1) through committed remove-3 and add-3 conf changes, then invoke Propose and ProposeConfChange on node 3 (bounded contexts, an unbounded context, and a retry cycle) and Propose on never-removed node 2 with the same leader, recording for each whether it returns, with which error, and whether its payload reaches any node's committed entries; finally force a leader change and observe both a new invocation and the still-pending context-free invocation.

knowledge.statement: While the run loop's proposal gate is disarmed for the re-added voter, a configuration change proposed through Node.ProposeConfChange is held pending in the same way as an ordinary proposal: the invocation had not returned after 800 ms (it released only at its own 900 ms deadline, with an empty error at that point) and no node applied a conf change adding the proposed node. The gate therefore covers the administrative entry point of the same member, not only ordinary proposals.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process, reliable per-sender delivery, no ticks; node 3 removed and re-added by committed conf changes with leader 1 unchanged; the proposed change is ConfChange add node 9, a node that is not part of the cluster.

interpretations.rationale: Five retained executions agree; this revision adds the administrative-entry-point case and leaves the earlier evidence unchanged. In 6e187216178a49d4ae02bd8c2afaeaf9: node 3 applied its own re-admission (index 4) and its configuration listed it as a voter with leader 1 (index 5); the witness invocation (index 6) had not returned after 1200 ms (index 7), released only at the caller's deadline (index 8: 'context deadline exceeded'), and left its payload absent (index 9); the context-free invocation was still pending after 2000 ms with its payload uncommitted (indices 11, 12); a configuration change proposed through node 3 (add node 9) had not returned after 800 ms (index 14: returned false, err empty, voter true, leader 1) and no node applied it (index 15: present false); the never-removed member's invocation returned in 0 ms and committed (indices 17, 18); two retries on node 3 (indices 20, 25) did not return while a proposal by node 2 committed in each interval (indices 23, 28); after the leader change a new invocation returned in 0 ms and committed (indices 31, 32), and the still-pending context-free invocation was admitted and committed (indices 33, 34). Source account: the run loop's gate variable is assigned only at node.go:374 (leader observed), 377 (no leader) and 426 (local member removed) and used as the receive case at node.go:386, and all MsgProp traffic - ordinary proposals and configuration changes alike, since ProposeConfChange routes through node.Step into the same wait (node.go:496-502) - is held pending on n.propc (node.go:525) while the gate is disarmed; a re-admission cannot match the removal guard because the local Progress entry is already gone (node.go:401-412). The snapshot's own expectation (node_test.go:352-385) scopes intended blocking to a node that does not know the current leader, which is not this case. Controls exclude cluster-wide stalls and a broken state machine, and indices 33/34 show the held request is eventually admitted and committed, so the defect is the interval itself: a member that is a voter with a healthy, known leader cannot get any proposal - ordinary or administrative - to a decision, and receives no error signal distinguishing this from a slow proposal.

knowledge.assertion: propc is armed only on observed leader change and is left nil after a re-admission
the caller sends on n.propc and stays pending while the run loop's gate variable is disarmed; a later observed leader change admits the pending request
the raft state machine returns ErrProposalDropped for a removed leader instead of blocking
intended blocking is scoped to the unknown-leader case and acceptance is expected once a leader is known; re-addition is untested
a configuration change proposed through the re-added voter was held pending and was not applied by any node

counterevidence: node.go:407-411 acknowledges the gate as improvised ('propc is reset when the leader changes ... This isn't very sound and likely has bugs'); this explains the dependence on leader changes but is neither a calling restriction nor a protection, and no other re-arm path exists in the snapshot.

node_test.go:352-385 shows that not returning is intended for a node that does not know the current leader. That expectation does not cover the witnessed case, and the same test expects acceptance once a leader is known.

No request is lost: held invocations are admitted unmodified once the gate is re-armed (indices 33, 34), so the harm is an unbounded wait without an error signal rather than data loss or a protocol safety violation.
The same runs contain successful paths (indices 17, 18, 23, 28, 32), showing proposals are neither generally dropped nor generally blocked.
limitations: Comparison outcomes for the earliest receipt were 'unknown' because that harness gave the three operations' result events the same names; its decisive events are complete and match the successor receipts, which have complete holds.

Scope is the async Node API path (node.run loop) in this snapshot; RawNode.Propose and RawNode.ProposeConfChange have no such gate. No ticks were delivered and delivery was reliable, so no timing or network-fault characterization is claimed.

Only the voter-removal form was executed; other transitions that delete the local Progress entry (for example a joint change that drops the node from both halves) are variants of the same cause and were not executed separately.

The configuration-proposal case was executed once with a single proposal (add node 9) and a single window; it establishes that the administrative entry point is affected, not a distribution over configuration-change kinds.
interpretations.joint_history: Five receipts from one fixed scenario lineage: 3592ccaf01864f56aaf06d54a3f97423-experiment (executed as 43a04622beef40588679c6cf1c40d6ad) and its successors 48ce57b251a644edaaf9d17731df0b25-experiment (a9f71d7a07454d058d818148f7479e8f), baee4030bf1e4f229c46ece8d0ddc365-experiment (87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4), de0272862d1842d2af26e89d955ed098-experiment (905d729b2a284c93bbbedd3c3a307ca8) and 5d5aaf795784463ea4d615854bbee98a-experiment (6e187216178a49d4ae02bd8c2afaeaf9), each registered with previous_id and a revision_reason. All five build the same configuration {1,2,3} from the same storage ConfState, elect leader 1 at term 1, apply the same committed remove-3 and add-3 conf changes on node 3, use the same witness/control/repair operation ids, payloads, phases, deadlines and windows, and force the same campaign of node 2 into term 2; the successors add event naming, then retry/progress cases, then the context-free and post-re-arm cases, then the configuration-proposal case, without altering the earlier ones. Witnesses agree field for field at the corresponding indices (witness 7/8/9 in all five; unbounded 11/12; control 15/16, 17/18 or 14/15 by receipt; repair 15/16, 25/26, 28/29 or 31/32), so the difference is a property of the fixed scenario rather than of one run.
